chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-'Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, who said:
I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'Allah never sent a prophet but He commanded him to prohibit alcohol, and that he should affirm for himself the doctrine of Al-Bada'.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (The title of Imam Musa al-Kadhim's son, Ali ibn Musa, the 8th Imam)
key_terms.الْبَدَاءِ: Al-Bada' (The doctrine of divine manifestation or appearance, where God reveals new rulings or changes destiny based on wisdom)
key_terms.الْخَمْرِ: Alcohol / Wine (specifically the drink prohibited in Islam)

ai.seo_question: What are the two key conditions Allah placed upon every prophet according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes 'Al-Bada'' as a universal condition of prophethood alongside the prohibition of khamr, linking practical legislation with core theological principles. In Shia scholarship, this affirms that divine knowledge is dynamic, allowing God to manifest new rulings or outcomes based on changing circumstances, a concept vital for understanding the evolution of Sharia and the Imams' authority. This hadith underscores the continuity between the practical prohibitions of the prophets and the metaphysical reality of divine decree.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 6. Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-`Alawi (rah) said, on the authority of `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt that
Al-Rida (AS) said: “Allah has never sent a prophet until he confirmed with Allah that he would forbid alcohol, and that he believed in Bada'.”
